description: The one obvious next step. Under monofocus a view has at most one primary action, so a button's emphasis is a claim about the screen rather than a decoration on the control.

MUST: Resolve every visual through its variant resolver from tokens, and expose that resolver so a custom control can speak the same language.
Keep the three axes separate: variant is tone and emphasis, size is geometry, state is the resolved state set.
Take its minimum height from density, and decouple visual size from hit target.
Use destructiveForeground on the destructive variant — never the brand ink as a stand-in.
Take the soft variant's ink from the brand ink verified against primarySoft, not from the brand surface.
Pair every enter with a faster exit, and animate press on the press-feedback role.
Fire a light impact haptic on activate, after commit rather than on request.
Carry a label when icon-only, and route its focus treatment through the shared focus ring.
SHOULD: Keep hover and press shifts derived — a lerp of the resting fill toward background or foreground — so they survive a palette change.
Use the soft variant as the mid-emphasis step when a screen needs brand colour without a second primary.
NEVER: Show two primary actions in one view. The second one is the answer to a question the screen has not asked.
Mint a state variant. There is no primaryDisabled and no smallGhost — states resolve inside the resolver.
Express danger with a status colour on primary. Danger is the destructive variant.
Hardcode a padding, a radius or a max width.
Ripple or flash a colour on press.
